text:
nina: new user hit weird behaviour on quickstart. first request returns 401, sdk retries with an updated token and then we see a billing banner in the console that made them think billing blocked the call.

nina: Repro steps they ran (local mac):
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_trial_temp
node quickstart.js
```

nina: Logs they pasted:
```
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] ERROR request id=1 status=401 Unauthorized
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] INFO sdk refreshing token and retrying (attempt 1)
[2026-03-21T09:12:02Z] INFO request id=1 status=200 OK
[2026-03-21T09:12:05Z] ERROR repeated failures detected, showing billing banner to user
```

carlos: hmm. looks like they used a short-lived trial key that was rotated by our onboarding flow. SDK does a refresh when it sees 401 (good), so the first call can fail then succeed. But the onboarding UX currently conflates repeated 4xx with billing-state checks, so banner appears prematurely.

pat: what confused the customer was the timing: they saw a 401 then a success, then the banner. they assumed billing blocked requests intermittently. they later opened support ticket.

support-bot: workspace "orchid-crew" is in trial and has automatic ephemeral trial keys enabled. billing not required for quickstarts but upgrade required for reserved capacity.

nina: customer flow suggestion: for quickstart we should document that the SDK will transparently refresh tokens and that an initial 401 can be transient. Also reduce the sensitivity of the onboarding banner so it doesn't trigger on a single-auth-retry pattern.

carlos: SDK note: maybe add local telemetry to detect "single 401 followed by immediate success" and avoid surfacing it as a billing problem. Also show clearer log: "401 received; attempting token refresh (likely ephemeral key expiration)".

pat: UX change: change banner copy to "Multiple request failures detected. If you see transient 401 then success, this may be token rotation for trial keys — confirm your API key or use a service account key."

nina: quick fix for user: recommend using a stable service account key for onboarding (we have a guide) or re-issue a non-ephemeral token from the console. For now they used a personal token and completed onboarding.

support-bot: created tickets: SDK-507 (improve 401 log + refresh transparency) and DOCS-945 (quickstart note about ephemeral keys).

carlos: additional thought: samples should default to reading REDWOOD_API_KEY from a `.env` or prompt so users notice ephemeral keys quickly. PR incoming to sample repo to add a short comment.

nina: will update the support reply and close after docs changes land. Thanks all :sparkles:
